candidates.title: The Value of Thinking: Learning When to Reason in Hybrid Decision Models
candidates.content: Existing adaptive-reasoning methods shorten the explicit reasoning a model writes, or skip it by switching modes; either way the answer is still written out token by token. Rather than deciding how much to think, we explore a different paradigm, zero-or-T thinking: a single model either answers from the implicit thinking inside one forward pass, generating no token, or performs full autoregressive reasoning at a cost of T tokens when that is worth paying. We realise it in a hybrid decision model (HDM), where one frozen backbone serves both modes and a lightweight self-routing block chooses between them. The block estimates the value of thinking, the utility the slow mode is expected to add over the fast one, from what that implicit thinking has already produced, and the slow mode runs only where that value exceeds a price λ set per request. Where no per-decision label exists, as in episodic agentic tasks, we introduce Calibrated Decision Policy Optimisation (CDPO), a reinforcement-learning recipe that trains the block from episode-level returns. candidates.title: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
candidates.content: Medical imaging is essential for diagnosing disease, guiding treatment and monitoring patients over time. Although artificial intelligence has advanced image interpretation, existing medical models often address restricted tasks, while general-purpose proprietary models lack access to private clinical imaging required to achieve medical expertise. Developing models that can interpret complex examinations and communicate their findings in the context of clinical decisions remains a major challenge. Here, we show that Neuro-VL, a vision-language model trained on nearly one million neuroimaging studies from routine clinical care, can interpret complete imaging examinations and engage in natural language conversations about their findings. Across internal and international datasets, Neuro-VL outperformed frontier general-purpose and specialized medical models in diagnosing, localizing, and describing abnormalities, as well as generating comprehensive radiology reports. The model also compared serial examinations to assess disease progression and more reliably resisted misleading clinical assumptions than leading frontier models from OpenAI and Google. candidates.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
candidates.content: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute. We find that the visual prior is not necessary; an encoder trained jointly from scratch is on par with a pretrained one, without a separate training stage. What matters instead is dedicated vision capacity: an encoder-free model trails on visual understanding even when its backbone is enlarged by the encoder's parameter count. candidates.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep with Claude
candidates.content: Our house has a box room, full of boxes that we still haven't unpacked from our last move. A couple of weeks ago something in that room started intermittently beeping . The beeps were far enough apart that standing in the room and trying to determine the source of the noise was frustrating, and I really didn't want to dig through every one of those boxes. So I had Claude Code build Beep Locator , a software system for triangulating the source of a mysterious beep using multiple devices scattered around the room. Here's what Beep Locator looks like after it has been running for a while: You run Python web server to show the primary UI, and then use the QR code or URL to connect as many devices as you can spare to act as listeners - I was using two iPads, a phone, a MacBook Pro and a Surface Ultra. The devices then play noises to each other to help estimate their locations. This didn't work particularly well, so I added a "Rough mode" where you can drag their icons around in the space to provide rough locations which are then adjusted based on those sounds. candidates.title: Quoting Prompting Claude Fable 5.2
candidates.content: Claude Fable 5.2 pays close attention to who owns the code it works on. In Anthropic’s testing on small coding tasks, the model tended to add to the existing structure when the prompt said nothing about ownership or presented the code base as someone else’s, even when that duplicated existing code. When the prompt said the code base was the model’s own, it often consolidated duplicated code and sometimes made related fixes without being asked. If you want the model to improve the structure as it works, say that the code is its own: You are the owner and long-term maintainer of this codebase, and its design is up to you. The ownership sentence makes the model much more likely to consolidate duplicated code into one shared function. In Anthropic’s testing on small coding tasks, the model consolidated duplicated code in under 10 percent of runs without the sentence and in about 75 percent of runs with it. — Prompting Claude Fable 5.2 , Anthropic documentation Tags: prompt-engineering , anthropic , generative-ai , ai , llms , claude-mythos-fable

candidates.title: Etiologies: Seeking Causation in Medicine and Poetry
candidates.content: One of the most central animating questions in medicine is “What is the cause?” Clinicians assiduously seek the diagnosis of a patient’s perplexing symptoms or probe what pathophysiology underlies the disease. Poetry is similarly engaged in a quest for knowing and by its enlarging of the field of inquiry as to the deepest roots of human suffering, it is complementary to, and thus useful in, medical practice. In the poem “Etiology,” medical language (“neoplastic transformation,” “terminology”) is placed beside unscientific explanatory systems (“feng shui,” “fortune stick[s]”), suggesting that illness may arise from several causal worlds at once. A malignancy may be cellular, environmental, familial, cultural, and even spiritual, depending on the kind of history being taken and by whom. “[A]bbreviations and poor penmanship” evokes the insufficiency patients may feel when their illness is summarily translated into clinical shorthand or technical jargon; poetry re-expands the diagnostic arena, restoring texture and richness to causation (“…white rice you relish/is it incense you burnt for your parents, black/on your fingertips blooming dust on the wall”). candidates.title: Neuroprotective Therapy for Acute Ischemic Stroke
candidates.content: A remarkable era in acute ischemic stroke care is now coming to a close—the period of the “reperfusion revolution.” Over the past few decades, pharmacological and mechanical flow restoration therapies became steadily more effective. By restoring blood flow and terminating the ischemic period, reperfusion salvages those cerebral tissues not yet irreversibly injured. However, the reperfusion strategy in acute stroke care is now reaching its limits. Current endovascular thrombectomy approaches reopen over 85% of occluded arteries, leaving little scope for further advance. And successful reperfusion treatment alone clearly only partially solves the therapeutic challenge. Among patients with ischemic stroke due to large-vessel occlusion who receive endovascular thrombectomy, more than two-thirds nevertheless have a disabled final outcome. Restoring blood flow yields incomplete recoveries because some irreversible injury accrues before recanalization can be achieved and additional injury is generated by reperfusion itself. candidates.title: Lifestyle and Metformin Interventions and Risk of Multimorbidity in Individuals With Prediabetes—In Reply
candidates.content: In Reply We thank Dr McCarthy and colleagues for their letter about our study, which demonstrated less multimorbidity among persons with prediabetes who underwent a lifestyle intervention. They raise the central implementation challenge of maintaining the essential components of an intervention that ensure its proven effectiveness while making necessary adaptations for real-world application. Incorporating new scientific findings that offer potentially short-term benefits must be done cautiously to avoid undermining the intervention’s long-term outcomes. We appreciate recent advances in pharmacotherapy, nutrition, and gut microbiome science and the evolving understanding of disease prevention. Although contemporary science has expanded available treatment modalities, lifestyle interventions continue to serve as a cornerstone of public health strategies for chronic disease prevention, with the behavior modification strategies to address energy balance remaining a core principle.

candidates.title: [Perspectives] Critical thinking about assisted dying
candidates.content: Assisted dying has been a hot political issue in the UK. The Scottish Parliament voted against it in March, 2026. The Isle of Man's Assisted Dying Bill received Royal Assent in October, 2026, but there is no date yet for its implementation. And in the UK Parliament, the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, introduced by Kim Leadbeater MP in 2024, was defeated in the House of Commons in September, 2026. Meanwhile, versions of assisted dying exist in many places, including Australia, Canada, New Zealand, in 14 jurisdictions in the USA, and some European countries such as Belgium, the Netherlands, and Switzerland.

candidates.title: Structure of a dopamine-binding RNA aptamer reveals metal-mediated ligand recognition
candidates.content: Abstract The selection of small-molecule-binding RNA aptamers enables the creation of ligand-responsive RNA tools, yet most aptamers fail to operate reliably across diverse environments. Scaffolded selection addresses this limitation by preserving the tertiary architecture of a riboswitch scaffold while driving the evolution of a new ligand-binding pocket. Using the purine riboswitch aptamer, we previously generated dopamine-binding aptamers. Here, we report the crystal structures of two representative variants in their apo and dopamine-bound states to define how they recognize ligand while maintaining scaffold integrity. The structures demonstrate that scaffolded selection enforces global fold conservation and retains the defining tertiary interactions of the parental riboswitch. Local remodeling, triggered by deletions acquired during selection, rewires the three-way junction to build extensive interaction networks that host the dopamine-binding pocket. A deeply buried potassium ion anchors ligand recognition, while the RNA engages the catechol ring through stacking and hydrogen bonding interactions. candidates.title: RecA protein activates the E. coli topoisomerase III catenation function: essential role of the RecA ATPase
candidates.content: Abstract RecA protein loaded into lesion-containing post-replication gaps must engage in strand exchange utilizing DNA substrates with no free ends, a process that is topologically constrained. The process can be mimicked by examining RecA-mediated DNA strand exchange between a circular ssDNA and a partially homologous circular supercoiled DNA. RecA protein can pair these substrates but cannot promote a net strand exchange. On its own, topoisomerase III promotes little reaction with the same two substrates. However, the two proteins together promote a robust reaction that rapidly, within 1–2 min, converts the substrates quantitatively to catenanes and hemicatenanes. The results reveal an important new functional interaction for bacterial topoisomerase III. The reaction is tightly coupled to RecA-mediated ATP hydrolysis. The rate of RecA-promoted ATP hydrolysis controls not just the extent but also the rate of the catenation/hemicatenation reaction. The ssDNA substrate is also required. Post-replication gaps are created in essentially every replication cycle and can be lethal if left unresolved. candidates.title: Hypernova: a faster and brighter light-producing deoxyribozyme
candidates.content: Abstract As a functional nucleic acid motif is optimized, better variants become less abundant in sequence space and significantly more difficult to identify. Here, we used two types of libraries to discover an improved variant of a previously optimized light-producing deoxyribozyme called Supernova. One library was designed in such a way that most mutations were consistent with the sequence requirements and secondary structure of this catalytic motif. The second contained short stretches of random sequence in place of AAAA spacers previously introduced in minimization experiments. Catalytically active sequences were isolated from each library using single and multiple round selections. Mutations from the best deoxyribozymes were then combined to yield an improved variant containing 12 mutations, which we named Hypernova. The rate of Hypernova at subsaturating substrate concentrations was up to 97-fold higher than that of Supernova, and its initial rate of light production was up to 30-fold faster. candidates.title: An anaerobic cell-free protein synthesis formulation for the in vitro study of oxygen sensitive proteins
candidates.content: Anaerobic microbes harbor unique enzymes and metabolic pathways with potential biotechnological applications, yet these microbes remain difficult to study and engineer. Research is limited by the labor-intensive workflows required to maintain anoxic environments and the lack of genetic tools available for non-model anaerobes. Here, we present an anaerobic cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) platform for the in vitro study of oxygen-sensitive enzymes. This study establishes two methods for conducting anaerobic CFPS, achieving an anoxic environment by (1) sparging with inert gas or (2) lyophilizing to remove oxygenated water. We show the functionality of our anaerobic CFPS formulation by producing oxygen-independent fluorescent protein reporters and a [4Fe-4S] cluster pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) with a specific activity of 5.2 {+/-} 0.3 x 10-4 U/{micro}L cell-free extract. This highly modular platform will allow study of diverse oxygen-sensitive proteins and requires only minor modifications to commonly used CFPS workflows.

candidates.title: Scalable recorders of cellular calcium dynamics and molecular interactions across time
candidates.content: Cellular processes are mediated by dynamic biochemical events in their native context, including changes in intracellular ion concentrations and transient interactions between molecules. Studying these processes across large cell populations requires recording their dynamics across time in single cells, simultaneously and at scale. Here, we introduce split-1POK, a split protein tape monomer whose two halves reconstitute when the domains fused to them interact. The reconstituted monomer is incorporated into the protein tape as it elongates across time in live cells, enabling scalable, spatiotemporally resolved endpoint readout under conventional light microscopy. Split-1POK provides a programmable scaffold for new recorders in the CytoSense family, our previously introduced framework (ref. 1) in which the same cytosol-localized monomer senses cellular activity and writes it along protein tape recorders. candidates.title: Antibody design across observed and forecasted antigenic evolution
candidates.content: The therapeutic efficacy of antibodies is often limited by the evolution of their targets. Designing or eliciting antibodies that withstand such evolution is challenging as their binding interfaces must accommodate antigenic variation. Here, we introduce Germinal Multi, a computational framework for de novo antibody design and rescue that jointly optimizes a single paratope against multiple antigenic variants. We applied Germinal Multi to cancer and viral antigens, targeting both observed antigenic variation and prospective antibody escape. Multi-target optimization yielded antibodies that bound resistance-associated EGFR variants or that neutralized antigenically distinct historical SARS-CoV-2 variants, with recognition extending to variants withheld from the design process. Beyond acting on observed evolution, we redesigned the broadly neutralizing antibody BD55-1205 to restore neutralization of a prospective escape variant engineered with guidance from an evolutionary forecasting model, while preserving activity against the parental variant. candidates.title: L-selectin shedding regulates post-infarction neutrophilia without altering myocardial injury or ventricular remodelling.
candidates.content: Myocardial infarction (MI) triggers rapid neutrophil mobilisation from the bone marrow (BM), resulting in systemic neutrophilia that is widely associated with myocardial injury. However, whether the magnitude of this response directly influences cardiac injury and subsequent ventricular remodelling remains unclear. Ectodomain shedding of L-selectin is a hallmark of neutrophil activation, although its contribution to neutrophil mobilisation following MI has not been established. Using mice expressing a non-cleavable L-selectin mutant (L(E)), we investigated the role of L-selectin shedding in post-MI neutrophilia. Under homeostatic conditions, WT and L(E) mice exhibited comparable BM neutrophil maturation and circulating neutrophil representation. Following permanent coronary ligation, however, L(E) mice exhibited markedly attenuated neutrophilia, associated with reduced circulating CXCL2 and decreased surface CXCR2 expression on BM neutrophils. Intravenous recombinant CXCL2 increased circulating neutrophil representation in WT but not L(E) mice, suggesting that impaired mobilisation cannot be explained solely by reduced ligand availability. candidates.title: Differential and Cooperative Immunomodulation by Saponin Adjuvants QS-21 and QS-7 in Human THP-1 Macrophages
candidates.content: QS-21, a triterpene glycoside saponin derived from Quillaja saponaria, is a potent immunostimulatory adjuvant incorporated in several FDA-approved vaccines. QS-7, a structurally related saponin fraction, has been reported to retain immunomodulatory activity with reduced hemolytic toxicity; however, its lower natural abundance has limited its systematic immunological characterization. To address this gap, we systematically compare responses to QS-21 and QS-7 in the THP-1 human macrophage model to resolve their distinct and cooperative contributions to antigen presenting cell (APC) activation. Following cytotoxicity profiling to establish safe and biologically relevant dosing, flow cytometry, proteomics, and transcriptomics were used to delineate the immunological programs engaged by each saponin alone and in combination. QS-7 alone induced minimal upregulation of cell surface activation markers and did not elicit a significant transcriptional signature, yet it drove dose-dependent secretion of a broad panel of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines, revealing a dissociation between these two arms of macrophage activation. candidates.title: Impact of vaccination coverage and timing on recent yellow fever outbreaks in Africa: a modeling study
candidates.content: Background: Multiple recent yellow fever (YF) outbreaks have occurred despite a highly effective vaccine. Increasing vaccination coverage and decreasing response times have been key components of the Eliminate Yellow Fever Epidemics (EYE) strategy. However, the combined impacts of these factors on YF outbreaks, especially since implementation of the EYE strategy in 2017, remain uncertain. Methods: We developed mathematical models to simulate the effects of vaccination coverage and timing, calibrating them to recent YF outbreaks in Ghana (2021-2022) and South Sudan (2023-2024). candidates.title: An agent-based model of Epstein-Barr virus transmission and vaccination
candidates.content: Epstein- Barr virus (EBV) infects over 90% of adults worldwide, causing infectious mononucleosis (IM) in adolescents and young adults and contributing to multiple malignancies. Despite its global burden, population- level transmission modeling of EBV remains limited. We present the first population- level agent-based model (ABM) of EBV transmission. The model is implemented with 10,000 agents and calibrated to age-specific seroprevalence data from the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey. Two complementary calibration methods are evaluated, each with its own distinct advantages: Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC) and Bayesian Optimization with Expected Quantile Improvement (BO- EQI). ABC directly yields an approximate distribution of transmission parameters for propagation through vaccination scenarios. BO- EQI uses a limited simulation budget to identify well-fitting parameter vectors, particularly as the number of fitted parameters increases. We estimate parameter uncertainty at each resolution in a separate Gaussian-kernel posterior analysis, which requires additional simulations and an explicit model for discrepancies between simulated and observed prevalence
